# Calcul des variances des fPC1{.tabset}

Après calcul des variances des fPC1, rangées par ordre décroissante, 
on se rend compte que le dju_refroi et le taux de possession de chat ont des variances très élevées et donc risque de oeser beaucoup dans le modèle GSCA. **La standardisation des variables est donc nécessaire.**

# Interprétation des fPC1{.tabset}

```{r, echo = FALSE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE}

# fonction pour extraire plus d'une composante fonctionelle

func_data <- function(data, Nb.Base, ncomp){

data <- data %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(annee = annee %>% factor, region = region %>%  factor)

# Paramètres
Temps      <- levels(data$annee)
NbTemps    <- length(Temps)
VarName    <- colnames(data)[-c(1:2)]
NbVar      <- length(VarName)
Regions    <- levels(data$region)
NbRegions  <- length(Regions)
my_palette <- colorRampPalette(c("blue", "grey", "red"))

# Transformation des variables en matrice
mat_tmps_reg <- lapply(1:NbVar, function(p) as.matrix(reshape2:::dcast(data, annee  ~ region, value.var = VarName[p])[, -1]))

# transformation en objet fonctionnel
# Base B-spline
spline.basis <- fda::create.bspline.basis(rangeval = c(0, 1), nbasis = Nb.Base, norder = 3)
# plot(spline.basis, lty = 1, lwd = 2, main = "Base de B-splines", xlab = 'Temps')
# Projection des données dans la base
data.amc.fd <- lapply(1:NbVar, function(p) {
  mat <- mat_tmps_reg[[p]]
  mat <- cbind(mat, annee = 2012:2024)
  mat <- na.omit(mat)
  Temps <- levels(as.factor(mat[, "annee"]))
  NbTemps    <- length(Temps)
  mat <- mat[,-which(colnames(mat) == "annee")]
  Time.01      <- seq(0, 1, length.out = NbTemps)
  fda::smooth.basis(Time.01, mat, spline.basis)$fd})

# fcpa
fPCA.amc <- lapply(1:NbVar, function(p) fda::pca.fd(data.amc.fd[[p]], nharm = ncomp, centerfns = TRUE))
names(fPCA.amc) <- VarName
df <- data.frame(col1 = rep(NA,12))
for (j in 1:NbVar){
  d <- as.data.frame(fPCA.amc[[j]]$scores)
  colnames(d) <- paste0(VarName[j], "_fPC", 1:ncol(d))
  df <- cbind.data.frame(df, d)
}
df <- df[,-1]
rownames(df) <- c("Auvergne-Rhone-Alpes", "Bourgogne-Franche-Comte", "Bretagne",               
"Centre-Val de Loire", "Grand Est", "Hauts-de-France", "IDF", "Normandie",               "Nouvelle-Aquitaine", "Occitanie", "PACA", "Pays de la Loire")
return(list(df, fPCA.amc))
}

```

## AMC{.tabset}

### log_AMC_EHPAD_C3G

- fPC1 (95.7 %): différence régions qui consomment beaucoup de C3G tout le temps (Nouvelle-Aquitaine) VS régions qui en consomment peu tous le temps (Pays de la Loire)
- fPC2 (2.8%): changement à partir de 2020 (covid), des régions consomment plus cette année là (IDF), ou après (Normandie, Auvergne Rhône Alpes)
- les scores fonctionnels n'ont pas l'air normalement distribués, elles semblent left skewed (surtout fPC1): **à réfléchir pour le bootstrap quelle autre loi peut convenir, peut-être faire des tests d'adéquation à une loi.**

```{r, echo = TRUE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE}

cols <- c("IDF" = "#FFD700", 
          "Auvergne-Rhone-Alpes" = "#FB6A4A", "PACA" = "#CB181D", 
          "Nouvelle-Aquitaine" = "#FD8D3C", "Occitanie" = "#D94701",
          "Centre-Val de Loire" = "#9ECAE1", "Pays de la Loire" = "#6BAED6",
          "Normandie" = "#3182BD", "Bretagne" = "#08519C", 
          "Bourgogne-Franche-Comte" = "#74C476", "Grand Est" = "#31A354", 
          "Hauts-de-France" = "#006D2C")

plot_fpca_gg <- function(pca_fd_obj, harm = 1, xlab = "Temps", title = NULL) {
  
  # Grille de temps
  t_grid <- seq(0, 1, length.out = 100)
  # Moyenne
  mean_vals <- fda::eval.fd(t_grid, pca_fd_obj$meanfd)
  # Fonction propre (harm-ième)
  harmfd   <- pca_fd_obj$harmonics[harm]
  harm_vals <- fda::eval.fd(t_grid, harmfd)
  # Variance expliquée
  varprop <- round(pca_fd_obj$varprop[harm] * 100, 1)
  # Amplitude de perturbation (comme plot.pca.fd)
  score_sd <- sqrt(pca_fd_obj$values[harm])
  
  df <- data.frame(
    t     = t_grid,
    mean  = mean_vals[, 1],
    plus  = mean_vals[, 1] + score_sd * harm_vals[, 1],
    minus = mean_vals[, 1] - score_sd * harm_vals[, 1]
  )
  
  if (is.null(title)) title <- paste0("fPC", harm, " (", varprop, "% var. exp.)")
  
  ggplot(df, aes(x = t)) +
    geom_line(aes(y = mean), color = "black", linewidth = 1) +
    geom_point(aes(y = plus), shape = 3, color = "black") +
    geom_line(aes(y = minus), color = "black", linewidth = 0.8, linetype = "dashed") +
    labs(title = title, x = xlab, y = "") +
    scale_x_continuous(
      breaks = seq(0, 1, length.out = 13),
      label = as.character(2012:2024)
      )+
    theme_bw()+
    theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 7),
          axis.text.y = element_text(color = "black", size = 6),
          axis.title = element_blank(),
          axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, vjust = 0.6, colour = "black", size = 6))
}

plot_comp_func <- function(data, variable){
g1 <- dat %>% 
  dplyr::select(region, annee, variable) %>% 
  tidyr::pivot_longer(!c("region", "annee"), names_to = "Var",
                      values_to = "value") %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = annee, y = value, col = region))+
  geom_point()+
  geom_line(show.legend = FALSE)+
  theme_bw()+
  labs(color = "Région",
       title = variable)+
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(2012, 2024, by = 1),
                     minor_breaks = seq(2012, 2024, by = 1))+
  theme(axis.text.y = element_text(size = 6, color = "black"),
        axis.title = element_blank(), 
        plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 7),
        axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, vjust = 0.6, colour = "black", size = 6), 
        legend.text = element_text(size = 6), 
        legend.title = element_text(size = 6),
        legend.position = "bottom",
        legend.justification = "left",
        legend.spacing = unit(0.5, "cm"),        
        legend.key.height = unit(0.1, "cm"),   
        legend.key.width = unit(0.1, "cm"),    
        legend.key.spacing.y = unit(0.1, "cm") 
        )+
  scale_color_manual(values = cols)


# Utilisation
p1 <- plot_fpca_gg(data[[2]][[variable]], harm = 1, xlab = "Temps")
p2 <- plot_fpca_gg(data[[2]][[variable]], harm = 2, xlab = "Temps")


p3 <- data[[1]] %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = .data[[paste0(variable,"_fPC1")]], 
             y = .data[[paste0(variable,"_fPC2")]]))+
  #geom_text(aes(label = rownames(data[[1]])), size = 1.8, vjust = -0.5)+
  geom_point(aes(col = rownames(data[[1]])), size = 1.3, show.legend = FALSE)+
  scale_x_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0.15, 0.15)))+
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0.15, 0.15)))+
  theme_bw()+
  labs(x = "fPC1", y = "fPC2", 
       title = "fPCA scores")+
  theme(axis.text = element_text(color = "black", size = 6),
        axis.title = element_text(size = 6), 
        plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 6))+
  scale_color_manual(values = cols)

p4 <- data[[1]] %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = .data[[paste0(variable,"_fPC1")]]))+
  geom_histogram(bins = 5, fill = "gold", color = "black", alpha = .5)+
  theme_bw()+
  labs(title = "Distribution fPC1")+
  theme(axis.text = element_text(color = "black", size = 6),
        axis.title.x = element_blank(), 
        plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 6), 
        axis.title.y = element_text(size = 6))

p5 <- data[[1]] %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = .data[[paste0(variable,"_fPC2")]]))+
  geom_histogram(bins = 5, fill = "gold", color = "black", alpha = .5)+
  theme_bw()+
  labs(title = "Distribution fPC2")+
  theme(axis.text = element_text(color = "black", size = 6),
        axis.title.x = element_blank(), 
        plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 6), 
        axis.title.y = element_text(size = 6))


combined <- g1 + p1 + p2 + p3 + p4 + p5
return(combined)
}

plot_comp_func(data = dat.func_EHPAD_C3G, variable = "log_AMC_EHPAD_C3G")

```

## Animals{.tabset}

### AMR_Animaux_compagnie_C3G

- Les trajectoires sont plus compliquées ici. Ce qui implique une baisse de % de variance exprimée par fPC1 et plus de variance expliquée par fPC2 que ce qu'on a pu voir auparavant. 
-fPC1: Les régions qui sont bien classées sont celles qui ont beaucoup de résistances aux C3G chez les animaux de compagnie sur une période de 2-3 ans (PACA 2018-2020, IDF 2012-2014, Pays de la Loire 2014-2015).
- fPC2: Les régions qui ont connu une recrudescense en résistance aux C3G chez les animaux de compagnie après 2016 sont bien classées selon fPC2 (PACA à partir de 2018, Normandie à partir de 2017), celles qui ont eu beaucoup de résistance aux début mais pour qui ça a baissé au cours du temps sont mal classées (IDF, Pays de la Loire).
- fPC1 semble avoir plus ou moins une distribution uniforme, fPC2 est right skewed.

```{r, echo = TRUE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE}

plot_comp_func(data = dat.func_ES_FQ, variable = "AMR_animaux_compagnie_C3G_R")

```

### AMR_Animaux_compagnie_FQ

-fPC1: Beaucoup de résistance en PACA et en IDF, peu de résistance en Centre Val de Loire et en Bourgogne Franche Comté de manière générale
-fPC2: les régions qui ont connu une augmentation de la résistance aux FQ après 2014 (IDF, PACA, BFC) VS celles qui ont connu une diminution après 2014 (Pays de la Loire, Occitanie).


### taux de possession de chats

- fPC1: régions qui ont beaucoup de chats tout le temps (Centre val de Loire, Nouvelle-Aquitaine, PACA) VS celles qui en ont moins (IDF, Auvergne-Rhone-Alpes).
- fPC2 concerne surtout IDF et PACA: stagnation du taux de possession de chats au cours du temps: l'IDF est le meilleur exemple, 3ème région avec le plus de chats en 2012, dernière en 2024, le PACA commence premier et finit 4ème.
- fPC1 légèrement right skewed et fPC2 très right skewed

```{r, echo = TRUE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE}
plot_comp_func(data = dat.func_EHPAD_FQ, variable = "tx_possession_chats")

```

### log_UGB_density_volailles

- le fPC1 résume casiment tout car il y a beaucoup de variabilité régionale mais peu de variabilité temporelle pour cette variable. régions rurales (Bretagne, Pays de la Loire) VS régions urbaines (PACA, IDF).


- fPC2: le fait d'avoir connu une augmentation de particules fines après 2018.

# Comparaison des régression GSCA{.tabset}

Le but ici, contrairement au Rmarkdown précédant, va être de considérer un modèle GSCA avec tous les blocs qui expliquent le block Y indépendamment, mais les blocks explicatifs ne s'expliquent pas entre eux. 

```{r, echo = F, warning = F, message = F, out.width='900px'}
knitr::include_graphics("C:/Users/g.martet/Documents/functional_study/modèle_sans_sous_modèle.png")
```

Nous allons également comparer ce modèle avec le modèle complet déjà effectué dans le Rmarkdown précédent et voir si les coefficients restent stables:

```{r, echo = F, warning = F, message = F, out.width='900px'}
knitr::include_graphics("C:/Users/g.martet/Documents/functional_study/update_relation_new_blocks.png")
```

En fonction de ce modèle complet, nous créerons un modèle intermédiaire avec moins de sous-modèle en supprimant les paths coeffs proches de 0. Nous en étudierons la stabilité et nous allons comparer les trois modèles

## AMR ville FQ{.tabset}

Les liens qui sont retirés pour le modèle intermédiaire sont Y ~ Animals et Y ~ Humans.

### Unidimensionalité des blocks

Le block AMC est unidimensionnel. Les blocks Environnement et Humains sont acceptables. Le block Animals ne semble pas unidimensionnel, cela peut-être du aux 4 variables dans le block au lieu de 2 pour les autres.

```{r, echo = TRUE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE}

source("C:/Users/g.martet/Documents/functional_study/explo_gesca.R")

dfPC1.AMR_ville_FQ <- scale(dfPC1.AMR_ville_FQ) # standardisation

# Hypothèse d'unidimensionalité des blocks
Xnorm.block <- list(dfPC1.AMR_ville_FQ[,which(colnames(dfPC1.AMR_ville_FQ) %in% c("log_AMC_ville_FQ", "log_AMC_ville_tot_except_FQ"))],
                    dfPC1.AMR_ville_FQ[,which(colnames(dfPC1.AMR_ville_FQ) %in% c("AMR_animaux_compagnie_FQ_R", "AMR_animaux_production_FQ_R", "tx_possession_chats", "log_UGB_density_livestock_tot"))],
                    dfPC1.AMR_ville_FQ[,which(colnames(dfPC1.AMR_ville_FQ) %in% c("air_PM25_pop", "dju_refroi"))],
                    dfPC1.AMR_ville_FQ[,which(colnames(dfPC1.AMR_ville_FQ) %in% c("medecin_hab", "unemployement_pourc"))]
                    )

nb.block <- length(Xnorm.block)
order_blocks <- c("AMC", "Animals", "Environment", "Humans")
eigen <- lapply(1:nb.block, function(k) FactoMineR::PCA(Xnorm.block[[k]], scale.unit = TRUE, ncp = 2, graph = F)$eig)
perc_var_comp1 <- c()
for(i in 1:nb.block){
  perc_var_comp1 <- c(perc_var_comp1, eigen[[i]][1,2])
}
df.unim <- data.frame(order_blocks, 
                      percentage_variance_PCA_comp1 = round(perc_var_comp1, 2))
knitr::kable(df.unim)


```

### Paths coeffs

Les paths coeffs ont l'air de varier assez peu entre le modèle complet et le modèle intermédiaire. 

En regardant le tableau, le modèle simple semble surestimer un peu le lien entre Y et AMC, Environnement par rapport au modèle complet et sous-estimer celui entre Y et Animals. Etonnament le modèle simple semble plus proche du modèle complet pour le lien entre Y et Humains que le modèle intermédiaire qui sous-estime un peu ce lien.

En regardant le graphique, les paths coeffs liés à Y semblent être estimés de manière plus précise avec le modèle intermédiaire. 

**Conclusion:** Le modèle complet ne semble pas apporter beaucoup plus d'information que le modèle intermédiaire. Le modèle intermédiaire est meilleur dans l'estimation des paths coeffs liés à Y. 

```{r, echo = TRUE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE}

model_simple <- paste(
  paste("Y =~", colnames(dfPC1.AMR_ville_FQ)[1]),
  "AMC =~ log_AMC_ES_FQ + log_AMC_ville_FQ",
  "Animals =~ AMR_animaux_compagnie_FQ_R + AMR_animaux_production_FQ_R + veto_by_AC + log_UGB_density_livestock_tot",
  "Environment =~ dju_refroi + air_PM25_pop",
  "Humans =~ medecin_hab + EQI_st",
  "Y ~ AMC + Animals + Environment + Humans",
  sep = "\n\t\t"
)

model_complet <- paste(
  paste("Y =~", colnames(dfPC1.AMR_ville_FQ)[1]),
  "AMC =~ log_AMC_ES_FQ + log_AMC_ville_FQ",
  "Animals =~ AMR_animaux_compagnie_FQ_R + AMR_animaux_production_FQ_R + veto_by_AC + log_UGB_density_livestock_tot",
  "Environment =~ dju_refroi + air_PM25_pop",
  "Humans =~ medecin_hab + EQI_st",
  "Y ~ AMC + Animals + Environment + Humans",
  "AMC ~ Humans + Environment",
  "Environment ~ Animals + Humans",
  "Humans ~ Environment + Animals",
  "Animals ~ Environment + Humans",
  sep = "\n\t\t"
)

model_int <- paste(
  paste("Y =~", colnames(dfPC1.AMR_ville_FQ)[1]),
  "AMC =~ log_AMC_ES_FQ + log_AMC_ville_FQ",
  "Animals =~ AMR_animaux_compagnie_FQ_R + AMR_animaux_production_FQ_R + veto_by_AC + log_UGB_density_livestock_tot",
  "Environment =~ dju_refroi + air_PM25_pop",
  "Humans =~ medecin_hab + EQI_st",
  "Y ~ AMC + Humans",
  "AMC ~ Humans + Environment",
  "Environment ~ Animals + Humans",
  "Humans ~ Environment + Animals",
  "Animals ~ Environment + Humans",
  sep = "\n\t\t"
)

set.seed(123)
mod_complet <- gesca::gesca.run(model_complet, dfPC1.AMR_ville_FQ, nbt = 100)
sum_gsca_complet <- summary_gesca2(mod_complet)
mod_simple <- gesca::gesca.run(model_simple, dfPC1.AMR_ville_FQ, nbt = 100)
sum_gsca_simple <- summary_gesca2(mod_simple)
mod_int <- gesca::gesca.run(model_int, dfPC1.AMR_ville_FQ, nbt = 100)
sum_gsca_int <- summary_gesca2(mod_int)

paths_complet <- sum_gsca_complet$paths
paths_complet$model <- rep("complet", nrow(paths_complet))
paths_simple <- sum_gsca_simple$paths
paths_simple$model <- rep("simple", nrow(paths_simple))
paths_int <- sum_gsca_int$paths
paths_int$model <- rep("int", nrow(paths_int))
paths <- rbind.data.frame(paths_complet, paths_simple, paths_int)

DT::datatable(paths)
```

```{r, echo = TRUE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE}

# 1. extraire la variable à expliquer (à gauche du ~)
paths$outcome <- str_remove(paths$term, "~.*")

# 2. créer une palette nommée par variable à expliquer
outcomes <- unique(paths$outcome)
pal <- setNames(c("#F8766D", "#00BF7D", "#E76BF3", 
                  "#A3A500", "#00B0F6"), outcomes)

# 3. vecteur de couleurs DANS L'ORDRE DES FACETTES
# (l'ordre des term tel qu'il apparaîtra dans facet_wrap, généralement alphabétique
# sauf si term est déjà un factor avec un ordre précis)
term_outcome_map <- setNames(paths$outcome, paths$term)
term_levels <- sort(unique(paths$term)) 
# applique 0.6 d'opacité à chaque couleur de la palette
pal_alpha <- scales::alpha(pal, 0.6)
strip_colors <- pal_alpha[term_outcome_map[term_levels]]


ggplot(paths, aes(x = model, y = estimate)) +
    geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = ci_lb, ymax = ci_ub, color = "95% CI"),
                   height = 0.1, alpha = 0.4) +
    geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = estimate - std.error,
                       ymax = estimate + std.error,
                       color = "+/- SE"),
                   height = 0.1, linewidth = 0.4, alpha = 0.4) +
    geom_point(aes(shape = model), size = 2) +
    geom_text(aes(label = round(estimate, 2)), size = 2, 
              vjust = -0.86)+
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
    ggh4x::facet_wrap2(~ term, scales = "free_y", 
                       strip = strip_themed(
      background_x = elem_list_rect(fill = strip_colors)
    ))+
    theme_bw() +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0.15, 0.25))) +
    labs(title = "Path coefficients with 95% CI and ±SE")+
    theme(axis.text = element_text(color = "black", size = 6),
          axis.title = element_blank(), 
          plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 7),
          strip.text = element_text(size = 6))+
  scale_color_manual(name = "Interval type",
                     values = c(
                       "95% CI" = "orange3",
                       "+/- SE" = "grey40"))

```

### R2

la qualité explicative des modèles complet et intermédiaire sont similaire. Le block Y est toutefois mieux expliqué avec le modèle simple.

```{r, echo = TRUE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE}

# corrélations entre composantes latentes
# complet
latentcorr_complet <- mod_complet$latentcorr  
rownames(latentcorr_complet) <- c("Y", "AMC", "Animals", "Environment", "Humans")
colnames(latentcorr_complet) <- c("Y", "AMC", "Animals", "Environment", "Humans")
# int
latentcorr_int <- mod_int$latentcorr  
rownames(latentcorr_int) <- c("Y", "AMC", "Animals", "Environment", "Humans")
colnames(latentcorr_int) <- c("Y", "AMC", "Animals", "Environment", "Humans")
# simple
latentcorr_simple <- mod_simple$latentcorr  
rownames(latentcorr_simple) <- c("Y", "AMC", "Animals", "Environment", "Humans")
colnames(latentcorr_simple) <- c("Y", "AMC", "Animals", "Environment", "Humans")

R2 <- data.frame(term = sum_gsca_complet$paths$term, 
                 R2_model_complet = rep(NA, length(sum_gsca_complet$paths$term)),
                 R2_model_int = rep(NA, length(sum_gsca_complet$paths$term)), 
                 R2_model_simple = rep(NA, length(sum_gsca_complet$paths$term)))

for (i in 1:nrow(R2)){
  # complet
  beta_comp_block <- sum_gsca_complet$paths$estimate[sum_gsca_complet$paths$term == R2$term[i]]
r_block_comp <- latentcorr_complet[stringr::str_split(R2$term[i], "~")[[1]][1], stringr::str_split(R2$term[i], "~")[[1]][2]]
R2[i,]$R2_model_complet <- beta_comp_block * r_block_comp
# intermédiaire
if (R2$term[i] %in% sum_gsca_int$paths$term){
beta_int_block <- sum_gsca_int$paths$estimate[sum_gsca_int$paths$term == R2$term[i]]
r_block_int <- latentcorr_int[stringr::str_split(R2$term[i], "~")[[1]][1], stringr::str_split(R2$term[i], "~")[[1]][2]]
R2[i,]$R2_model_int <- beta_int_block * r_block_int}
else {R2[i,]$R2_model_int <- NA}
# simple
if (R2$term[i] %in% sum_gsca_simple$paths$term){
beta_simple_block <- sum_gsca_simple$paths$estimate[sum_gsca_simple$paths$term == R2$term[i]]
r_block_simple <- latentcorr_simple[stringr::str_split(R2$term[i], "~")[[1]][1], stringr::str_split(R2$term[i], "~")[[1]][2]]
R2[i,]$R2_model_simple <- beta_simple_block * r_block_simple}
else {R2[i,]$R2_model_simple <- NA}
}

knitr::kable(R2, digits = 2)

# Les R2 par blocs
r2 <- data.frame(
  var = c("Y", "AMC", "Animals", "Environment", "Humans"),
  R2_model_complet = round(mod_complet$R2[1,], 2),
  R2_model_int = round(mod_int$R2[1,], 2),
  R2_model_simple = round(mod_simple$R2[1,], 2)
)

knitr::kable(r2)
```

### FIT

- FIT est le fit global du modèle qui prends en compte tout les paramètres. **ici il est équivalent entre le modèle intermédiaire et le modèle complet.**

- AFIT est l'équivalent en régression du R^2 ajusté. c'est un FIT corrigé par le nombre de paramètres à estimer du modèle. **Dans notre cas, avec 12 régions et beaucoup de paramètres, il vaut mieux considérer cet indicateur que le FIT. Il est meilleur pour le modèle intermédiaire mais modéremment, il vaut 0.54.**

- le FIT_M est l'équivalent du R^2 pour le modèle de mesure, c'est-à-dire le modèle qui passe des variables latentes aux variables d'origine, il est ici équivalent entre les trois modèles. 

- le FIT_S est l'équivalent du R^2 pour le modèle structurel, c'est-à-dire les liens linéaires entre les variables latentes et les paths coeffs. **Il est élevé et équivalent entre le modèle complet et le modèle intermédiaire. Il est forcément bien plus faible pour le modèle simple car, celui-ci comprends moins de leins entre les blocks à expliquer.**

- Le GFI et le SRMR sont des mesures qui permettent d'estimer à quel point un modèle modélise bien la covariance des données en considérant tous les paramètres. En théorie d'après *Generalized structured component analysis: A Component-Based Approach to Structural Equation Modeling (pp.26-32)* (Hwang & Takane, 2014), le GFI doit être le plus proche de 1 possible (idéalement > 0.90) et me SRMR doit être le plus proche de 0 possible (< 0.04). **Ici il n'y a que le modèle simple qui est bon en termes de GFI, et le SRMR est mauvais pour les trois modèles.**


```{r, echo = TRUE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE}

fit_complet <- featmeasures2(mod_complet)
fit_complet$model <- rep("complet", nrow(fit_complet))
fit_simple <- featmeasures2(mod_simple)
fit_simple$model <- rep("simple", nrow(fit_simple))
fit_int <- featmeasures2(mod_int)
fit_int$model <- rep("int", nrow(fit_int))
fit <- rbind.data.frame(fit_complet, fit_simple, fit_int)

DT::datatable(fit)
```

### Coefficients de régression

**On considère ici seulement le modèle intermédaire car c'est celui-là qu'on a choisi de présenter.**

Comme ce qu'on a pu déjà constater en regardant le graphe. Ce n'est pas la consommation d'antibiotique sur la même année qui a l'air de jouer principalement sur la résisantce aux fluoroquinolones. Mais plutôt le nombre de médecin par habitants et l'EQI. Visiblement, le nombre de medecin s'explique par si la région est urbaine ou rurale (beaucoup de pollution et peu d'animaux de production impliquent beaucoup de médecins parce que région urbanisée) et l'EQI aussi mais à l'inverse.


```{r, echo = TRUE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE}

Matrix_reg <- function(model_type){

beta <- paths %>% dplyr::filter(model == model_type) %>% 
  dplyr::select(term, estimate)
w <- weights %>% dplyr::filter(model == model_type) %>% 
  dplyr::select(term, estimate, block) 
p <- loadings %>% dplyr::filter(model == model_type) %>% 
  dplyr::select(term, estimate, block) 

nrow(beta)
nrow(p)
nrow(w)

M <- matrix(rep(0, length(p$term)^2), nrow = length(p$term), ncol = length(p$term))
rownames(M) <- p$term
colnames(M) <- p$term

for (bl in levels(factor(p$block))){
  idx <- which(stringr::str_remove(beta$term, "~.*") == bl)
  beta_chosen <- beta[idx,]
  w_choosen <- w[which(w$block %in% str_remove(beta[idx,]$term, ".*~")),]
  
  beta_chosen$block <- str_remove(beta_chosen$term, ".*~")
  
  # loadings du bloc CIBLE (fixes pour tout bl, ne dépendent pas de b)
  p_bl <- p[p$block == bl,]
  is <- which(rownames(M) %in% p_bl$term)
  pp <- p_bl$estimate   # même ordre que rownames(M)[is]
  
  for (b in beta_chosen$block){
    js <- which(colnames(M) %in% w_choosen[w_choosen$block == b,]$term)
    ww <- w_choosen[w_choosen$block == b,]$estimate
    bb <- beta_chosen[beta_chosen$block == b,]$estimate
    
    M[is, js] <- bb * pp %*% t(ww)
  }
}

return(M)}

M <- Matrix_reg(model_type = "int")

cl <- as.data.frame(correspondance_block[which(correspondance_block$term %in% colnames(M)),])
cl <- rbind.data.frame(cl,
data.frame(block = "Y", term = "AMR_ville_FQ_R"))
rownames(cl) <- cl$term
cl <- cl %>% dplyr::select(-term)

disp <- matrix(sprintf("%.2f", M), nrow = nrow(M), ncol = ncol(M))
disp[abs(M) == 0] <- ""

ann_colors <- list(
 block = c(
    Y = "#F8766D",
    Animals = "#00B0F6",
    Humans = "#E76BF3",
    Environment = "#00BF7D",
    AMC = "#A3A500"
  )
)

ph <- pheatmap::pheatmap(M,
                          color = colorRampPalette(c("blue", "grey80", "red"))(100),
                          breaks = seq(-1, 1, length.out = 101),
                          cluster_rows = FALSE,
                          cluster_cols = FALSE,
                          # clustering_distance_rows = "euclidean",
                          # clustering_distance_cols = "euclidean",
                          # clustering_method = "ward.D2",  
                          number_format = "%.1f",
                          fontsize = 7,
                          number_color = "white",
                          legend = TRUE,
                          legend_breaks = c(-1, -0.5, 0, 0.5, 1),
                          legend_labels = c("-1", "-0.5", "0", "0.5", "1"),
                          angle_col = 90,
                          annotation_row = cl, 
                          annotation_col = cl,
                          annotation_colors = ann_colors,
                          display_numbers = disp,
                          main = "Regression coefficient")

ggsave("C:/Users/g.martet/Documents/Agrostat Dijon/figures/coeff_reg_AMR_ville_FQ.png", plot = ph, width = 7, height = 5)
```

### Regression Ridge VL

```{r, echo = TRUE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE}


submodels <- c("Y ~ AMC + Humans",
  "AMC ~ Humans + Environment",
  "Environment ~ Animals + Humans",
  "Humans ~ Environment + Animals",
  "Animals ~ Environment + Humans")

tab_ridge <- sum_gsca_int$paths %>% 
  dplyr::select(term, path_coeff = estimate) %>% 
  dplyr::arrange(desc(term))

get_ridge_betas <- function(formula_str, data) {
  parts <- strsplit(formula_str, "~")[[1]]
  response <- trimws(parts[1])
  predictors <- trimws(strsplit(parts[2], "\\+")[[1]])
  
  x <- as.matrix(data[, predictors, drop = FALSE])
  y <- data[,response]
  
  set.seed(123)
  cv_ridge <- cv.glmnet(x, y, alpha = 0)
  best_lambda <- cv_ridge$lambda.min
  out.ridge <- glmnet(x, y, alpha = 0, lambda = best_lambda)
  
  betas <- as.matrix(out.ridge$beta)
  
  data.frame(
    term = paste0(response, "~", predictors),
    ridge_beta = as.numeric(betas),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
}

# Application à tous les submodels + assemblage
ridge_results <- purrr::map_dfr(submodels, get_ridge_betas, data = latent_coord)

# Jointure avec ton tableau initial
tab_ridge <- tab_ridge %>%
  dplyr::left_join(ridge_results, by = "term")

knitr::kable(tab_ridge, digits = 2)

# scatterplot VL avec les betas normaux et ridge
make_scatter2 <- function(term, tab_ridge) {
  vars <- str_split(term, "~")[[1]]
  yvar <- vars[1]
  xvar <- vars[2]
  form <- paste0(yvar, "~", xvar)
  
  ggplot(df_coord, aes(x = .data[[xvar]], y = .data[[yvar]], col = id)) +
    geom_point(size = 1.6) +
    theme_bw() +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, col = "grey50", linetype = "dashed") +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0, col = "grey50", linetype = "dashed") +
    geom_abline(aes(intercept = 0, slope = tab_ridge[tab_ridge$term == form, "path_coeff"],
                     linetype = "path_coeff"),
                color = "black", key_glyph = "path") +
    geom_abline(aes(intercept = 0, slope = tab_ridge[tab_ridge$term == form, "ridge_beta"],
                     linetype = "ridge"),
                color = "black", key_glyph = "path") +
    scale_linetype_manual(name = NULL, 
                           values = c("path_coeff" = "solid", "ridge" = "twodash")) +
    theme(legend.title = element_blank(), 
          axis.text = element_text(color = "black", size = 6.5), 
          axis.title = element_text(size = 6.5), 
          legend.text = element_text(size = 6.5),
          plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 6.5),
        legend.position = "bottom",
        legend.spacing = unit(0.5, "cm"),        
        legend.key.height = unit(0.1, "cm"),   
        legend.key.width = unit(0.1, "cm"),    
        legend.key.spacing.y = unit(0.1, "cm")) +
    scale_color_manual(values = cols) +
    labs(title = term, x = xvar, y = yvar)
}
```

### Unidimensionalité des blocks 

On peut supposer que le block AMC est unidimensionnel.

```{r, echo = TRUE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE}

dfPC1.AMR_EHPAD_FQ <- scale(dfPC1.AMR_EHPAD_FQ) # standardisation

# Hypothèse d'unidimensionalité des blocks
Xnorm.block <- list(dfPC1.AMR_EHPAD_FQ[,which(colnames(dfPC1.AMR_EHPAD_FQ) %in% c("log_AMC_EHPAD_FQ", "log_AMC_ES_totale", "log_AMC_ville_totale"))],
                    dfPC1.AMR_EHPAD_FQ[,which(colnames(dfPC1.AMR_EHPAD_FQ) %in% c("AMR_animaux_production_FQ_R", "veto_by_AC", "tx_possession_chats", "log_UGB_density_livestock_tot"))],
                    dfPC1.AMR_EHPAD_FQ[,which(colnames(dfPC1.AMR_EHPAD_FQ) %in% c("air_PM25_pop", "dju_refroi"))],
                    dfPC1.AMR_EHPAD_FQ[,which(colnames(dfPC1.AMR_EHPAD_FQ) %in% c("medecin_hab", "pop_75_plus_prop"))]
                    )

nb.block <- length(Xnorm.block)
order_blocks <- c("AMC", "Animals", "Environment", "Humans")
eigen <- lapply(1:nb.block, function(k) FactoMineR::PCA(Xnorm.block[[k]], scale.unit = TRUE, ncp = 2, graph = F)$eig)
perc_var_comp1 <- c()
for(i in 1:nb.block){
  perc_var_comp1 <- c(perc_var_comp1, eigen[[i]][1,2])
}
df.unim <- data.frame(order_blocks, 
                      percentage_variance_PCA_comp1 = round(perc_var_comp1, 2))
knitr::kable(df.unim)


```

```{r, echo = TRUE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE}
                   height = 0.1, alpha = 0.4) +
    geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = estimate - std.error,
                       ymax = estimate + std.error,
                       color = "+/- SE"),
                   height = 0.1, linewidth = 0.4, alpha = 0.4) +
    geom_point(aes(shape = model), size = 2) +
    geom_text(aes(label = round(estimate, 2)), size = 2,
              vjust = -0.86)+
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
  ggh4x::facet_wrap2(~ term, scales = "free", 
                       strip = strip_themed(
      background_x = elem_list_rect(fill = strip_colors)
    ))+
    theme_bw() +
    labs(title = "Path coefficients with 95% CI and ±SE")+
    theme(axis.text = element_text(color = "black", size = 6),
          axis.title = element_blank(), 
          plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 7),
          strip.text = element_text(size = 6))+
  scale_color_manual(name = "Interval type",
                     values = c(
                       "95% CI" = "orange3",
                       "+/- SE" = "grey40"))

```

### Loadings

Les variables des blocks Environnement et AMC sont stables en termes de loadings. Mais pas celles des blocks Humans et Animals, le modèle simple sous-estime ou sur-estime les loadings à chaque fois pour ces variables là, par rapport au modèle complet.

### Poids

- Dans le block "Animals" Le modèle simple donne plus d'importance à la résisantance aux FQ chez les animaux de production, le modèle complet en donne moins à cette variable là et plus aux autres variables.

- Le modèle simple donne moins d'importance au vieillissement de la population et plus d'importance aux nombre de médecins par habitants. 

- Pour l'instant, on peut dire que ce sont surtout les blocks Animals et Humans qui différencient les deux modèles.

### R2

Forcément, on ne peut comparer que le Y et il a l'air un peu meilleur avec le modèle simple.

```{r, echo = TRUE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE}

# corrélations entre composantes latentes
# complet
latentcorr_complet <- mod_complet$latentcorr  
rownames(latentcorr_complet) <- c("Y", "AMC", "Animals", "Environment", "Humans")
colnames(latentcorr_complet) <- c("Y", "AMC", "Animals", "Environment", "Humans")
# simple
latentcorr_simple <- mod_simple$latentcorr  
rownames(latentcorr_simple) <- c("Y", "AMC", "Animals", "Environment", "Humans")
colnames(latentcorr_simple) <- c("Y", "AMC", "Animals", "Environment", "Humans")

R2 <- data.frame(term = sum_gsca_complet$paths$term, 
                 R2_model_complet = rep(NA, length(sum_gsca_complet$paths$term)),
                 R2_model_simple = rep(NA, length(sum_gsca_complet$paths$term)))

for (i in 1:nrow(R2)){
  # complet
  beta_comp_block <- sum_gsca_complet$paths$estimate[sum_gsca_complet$paths$term == R2$term[i]]
r_block_comp <- latentcorr_complet[stringr::str_split(R2$term[i], "~")[[1]][1], stringr::str_split(R2$term[i], "~")[[1]][2]]
R2[i,]$R2_model_complet <- beta_comp_block * r_block_comp
# simple
if (R2$term[i] %in% sum_gsca_simple$paths$term){
beta_simple_block <- sum_gsca_simple$paths$estimate[sum_gsca_simple$paths$term == R2$term[i]]
r_block_simple <- latentcorr_simple[stringr::str_split(R2$term[i], "~")[[1]][1], stringr::str_split(R2$term[i], "~")[[1]][2]]
R2[i,]$R2_model_simple <- beta_simple_block * r_block_simple}
else {R2[i,]$R2_model_simple <- NA}
}

knitr::kable(R2, digits = 2)


# Les R2 par blocs
r2 <- data.frame(
  var = c("Y", "AMC", "Animals", "Environment", "Humans"),
  R2_model_complet = round(mod_complet$R2[1,], 2),
  R2_model_simple = round(mod_simple$R2[1,], 2)
)

knitr::kable(r2)
```

## AMR_ES_FQ_R{.tabset}

Etonnament, le path coeff de Y ~ AMC est très faible (égal à 0,05), nous considérons donc un modèle intermédiaire sans. 

### Unidimensionalité des blocks 

On peut supposer que le block AMC est unidimensionnel.

```{r, echo = TRUE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE}

log_AMC_ES_FQ <- dfPC1.AMR_ES_C3G$log_AMC_ES_FQ
dfPC1.AMR_ES_FQ <- cbind.data.frame(dfPC1.AMR_ES_FQ, log_AMC_ES_FQ)
dfPC1.AMR_ES_FQ <- dfPC1.AMR_ES_FQ %>%
  dplyr::relocate(log_AMC_ES_FQ, .before = log_AMC_ES_totale)

dfPC1.AMR_ES_FQ <- scale(dfPC1.AMR_ES_FQ) # standardisation

# Hypothèse d'unidimensionalité des blocks
Xnorm.block <- list(dfPC1.AMR_ES_FQ[,which(colnames(dfPC1.AMR_ES_FQ) %in% c("log_AMC_ES_FQ", "log_AMC_ville_FQ"))],
                    dfPC1.AMR_ES_FQ[,which(colnames(dfPC1.AMR_ES_FQ) %in% c("AMR_animaux_compagnie_C3G_R", "tx_possession_chats", "log_UGB_density_livestock_tot"))],
                    dfPC1.AMR_ES_FQ[,which(colnames(dfPC1.AMR_ES_FQ) %in% c("air_PM25_pop", "dju_refroi"))],
                    dfPC1.AMR_ES_FQ[,which(colnames(dfPC1.AMR_ES_FQ) %in% c("medecin_hab", "pop_75_plus_prop", "EQI_st"))]
                    )

nb.block <- length(Xnorm.block)
order_blocks <- c("AMC", "Animals", "Environment", "Humans")
eigen <- lapply(1:nb.block, function(k) FactoMineR::PCA(Xnorm.block[[k]], scale.unit = TRUE, ncp = 2, graph = F)$eig)
perc_var_comp1 <- c()
for(i in 1:nb.block){
  perc_var_comp1 <- c(perc_var_comp1, eigen[[i]][1,2])
}
df.unim <- data.frame(order_blocks, 
                      percentage_variance_PCA_comp1 = round(perc_var_comp1, 2))
knitr::kable(df.unim)


```


### Path coeff

Le modèle intermédiaire semble surestimer les paths coeffs par rapport au modèle complet nottament pour les sous-modèles. Le modèle simple semble être plus précis pour estimer les liens avec les Y.

```{r, echo = TRUE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE}

model_simple <- paste(
  paste("Y =~", colnames(dfPC1.AMR_ES_FQ)[1]),
  "AMC =~ log_AMC_ES_FQ + log_AMC_ville_FQ",
  "Animals =~ AMR_animaux_compagnie_C3G_R + tx_possession_chats + log_UGB_density_livestock_tot",
  "Environment =~ dju_refroi + air_PM25_pop",
  "Humans =~ medecin_hab + pop_75_plus_prop + EQI_st",
  "Y ~ AMC + Animals + Environment + Humans",
  sep = "\n\t\t"
)

model_complet <- paste(
  paste("Y =~", colnames(dfPC1.AMR_ES_FQ)[1]),
  "AMC =~ log_AMC_ES_FQ + log_AMC_ville_FQ",
  "Animals =~ AMR_animaux_compagnie_C3G_R + tx_possession_chats + log_UGB_density_livestock_tot",
  "Environment =~ dju_refroi + air_PM25_pop",
  "Humans =~ medecin_hab + pop_75_plus_prop + EQI_st",
  "Y ~ AMC + Animals + Environment + Humans",
  "AMC ~ Humans + Environment",
  "Environment ~ Animals + Humans",
  "Humans ~ Environment + Animals",
  "Animals ~ Environment + Humans",
  sep = "\n\t\t"
)

model_int <- paste(
  paste("Y =~", colnames(dfPC1.AMR_ES_FQ)[1]),
  "AMC =~ log_AMC_ES_FQ + log_AMC_ville_FQ",
  "Animals =~ AMR_animaux_compagnie_C3G_R + tx_possession_chats + log_UGB_density_livestock_tot",
  "Environment =~ dju_refroi + air_PM25_pop",
  "Humans =~ medecin_hab + pop_75_plus_prop + EQI_st",
  "Y ~ Animals + Environment + Humans",
  "AMC ~ Humans + Environment",
  "Environment ~ Animals + Humans",
  "Humans ~ Environment + Animals",
  "Animals ~ Environment + Humans",
  sep = "\n\t\t"
)

set.seed(123)
mod_complet <- gesca::gesca.run(model_complet, dfPC1.AMR_ES_FQ, nbt = 100)
sum_gsca_complet <- summary_gesca2(mod_complet)
mod_simple <- gesca::gesca.run(model_simple, dfPC1.AMR_ES_FQ, nbt = 100)
sum_gsca_simple <- summary_gesca2(mod_simple)
mod_int <- gesca::gesca.run(model_int, dfPC1.AMR_ES_FQ, nbt = 10)
sum_gsca_int <- summary_gesca2(mod_int)


paths_complet <- sum_gsca_complet$paths
paths_complet$model <- rep("complet", nrow(paths_complet))
paths_simple <- sum_gsca_simple$paths
paths_simple$model <- rep("simple", nrow(paths_simple))
paths_int <- sum_gsca_int$paths
paths_int$model <- rep("int", nrow(paths_int))
paths <- rbind.data.frame(paths_complet, paths_simple, paths_int)

DT::datatable(paths)
```

```{r, echo = TRUE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE}

paths$outcome <- str_remove(paths$term, "~.*")

outcomes <- unique(paths$outcome)
pal <- setNames(c("#F8766D", "#00BF7D", "#E76BF3", 
                  "#A3A500", "#00B0F6"), outcomes)

term_outcome_map <- setNames(paths$outcome, paths$term)
term_levels <- sort(unique(paths$term)) 
# applique 0.6 d'opacité à chaque couleur de la palette
pal_alpha <- scales::alpha(pal, 0.6)
strip_colors <- pal_alpha[term_outcome_map[term_levels]]


ggplot(paths, aes(x = model, y = estimate)) +
    geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = ci_lb, ymax = ci_ub, color = "95% CI"),
                   height = 0.1, alpha = 0.4) +
    geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = estimate - std.error,
                       ymax = estimate + std.error,
                       color = "+/- SE"),
                   height = 0.1, linewidth = 0.4, alpha = 0.4) +
    geom_point(aes(shape = model), size = 2) +
    geom_text(aes(label = round(estimate, 2)), 
              size = 2, vjust = -0.86)+
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
    ggh4x::facet_wrap2(~ term, scales = "free", 
                       strip = strip_themed(
      background_x = elem_list_rect(fill = strip_colors)
    ))+
    theme_bw() +
    labs(title = "Path coefficients with 95% CI and ±SE")+
    theme(axis.text = element_text(color = "black", size = 6),
          axis.title = element_blank(), 
          plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 7),
          strip.text = element_text(size = 6))+
  scale_color_manual(name = "Interval type",
                     values = c(
                       "95% CI" = "orange3",
                       "+/- SE" = "grey40"))
```

### R2

Le modèle intermédiaire et lemodèle complet donnent les mêmes résultats de performance des sous-modèles. Le modèle simple est un tout petit peu mieux pour le modèle principal

```{r, echo = TRUE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE}

# corrélations entre composantes latentes
# complet
latentcorr_complet <- mod_complet$latentcorr  
rownames(latentcorr_complet) <- c("Y", "AMC", "Animals", "Environment", "Humans")
colnames(latentcorr_complet) <- c("Y", "AMC", "Animals", "Environment", "Humans")
# int
latentcorr_int <- mod_int$latentcorr  
rownames(latentcorr_int) <- c("Y", "AMC", "Animals", "Environment", "Humans")
colnames(latentcorr_int) <- c("Y", "AMC", "Animals", "Environment", "Humans")
# simple
latentcorr_simple <- mod_simple$latentcorr  
rownames(latentcorr_simple) <- c("Y", "AMC", "Animals", "Environment", "Humans")
colnames(latentcorr_simple) <- c("Y", "AMC", "Animals", "Environment", "Humans")

R2 <- data.frame(term = sum_gsca_complet$paths$term, 
                 R2_model_complet = rep(NA, length(sum_gsca_complet$paths$term)),
                 R2_model_int = rep(NA, length(sum_gsca_complet$paths$term)), 
                 R2_model_simple = rep(NA, length(sum_gsca_complet$paths$term)))

for (i in 1:nrow(R2)){
  # complet
  beta_comp_block <- sum_gsca_complet$paths$estimate[sum_gsca_complet$paths$term == R2$term[i]]
r_block_comp <- latentcorr_complet[stringr::str_split(R2$term[i], "~")[[1]][1], stringr::str_split(R2$term[i], "~")[[1]][2]]
R2[i,]$R2_model_complet <- beta_comp_block * r_block_comp
# intermédiaire
if (R2$term[i] %in% sum_gsca_int$paths$term){
beta_int_block <- sum_gsca_int$paths$estimate[sum_gsca_int$paths$term == R2$term[i]]
r_block_int <- latentcorr_int[stringr::str_split(R2$term[i], "~")[[1]][1], stringr::str_split(R2$term[i], "~")[[1]][2]]
R2[i,]$R2_model_int <- beta_int_block * r_block_int}
else {R2[i,]$R2_model_int <- NA}
# simple
if (R2$term[i] %in% sum_gsca_simple$paths$term){
beta_simple_block <- sum_gsca_simple$paths$estimate[sum_gsca_simple$paths$term == R2$term[i]]
r_block_simple <- latentcorr_simple[stringr::str_split(R2$term[i], "~")[[1]][1], stringr::str_split(R2$term[i], "~")[[1]][2]]
R2[i,]$R2_model_simple <- beta_simple_block * r_block_simple}
else {R2[i,]$R2_model_simple <- NA}
}

knitr::kable(R2, digits = 2)



# Les R2 par blocs
r2 <- data.frame(
  var = c("Y", "AMC", "Animals", "Environment", "Humans"),
  R2_model_complet = round(mod_complet$R2[1,], 2),
  R2_model_int = round(mod_int$R2[1,], 2),
  R2_model_simple = round(mod_simple$R2[1,], 2)
)

knitr::kable(r2)
```

## AMR EHPAD C3G{.tabset}

### Unidimensionalité des blocks

Le block "Animals" n'a pas l'air unidimensionnel.

```{r, echo = TRUE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE}

dfPC1.AMR_EHPAD_C3G <- scale(dfPC1.AMR_EHPAD_C3G) # standardisation

# Hypothèse d'unidimensionalité des blocks
Xnorm.block <- list(dfPC1.AMR_EHPAD_C3G[,which(colnames(dfPC1.AMR_EHPAD_C3G) %in% c("log_AMC_EHPAD_C3G", "log_AMC_ville_totale"))],
                    dfPC1.AMR_EHPAD_C3G[,which(colnames(dfPC1.AMR_EHPAD_C3G) %in% c("AMR_animaux_production_C3G_R", "tx_possession_chats", "tx_possession_chevaux", "log_UGB_density_volailles"))],
                    dfPC1.AMR_EHPAD_C3G[,which(colnames(dfPC1.AMR_EHPAD_C3G) %in% c("air_PM25_pop", "dju_refroi"))],
                    dfPC1.AMR_EHPAD_C3G[,which(colnames(dfPC1.AMR_EHPAD_C3G) %in% c("medecin_hab", "pop_75_plus_prop"))]
                    )

nb.block <- length(Xnorm.block)
order_blocks <- c("AMC", "Animals", "Environment", "Humans")
eigen <- lapply(1:nb.block, function(k) FactoMineR::PCA(Xnorm.block[[k]], scale.unit = TRUE, ncp = 2, graph = F)$eig)
perc_var_comp1 <- c()
for(i in 1:nb.block){
  perc_var_comp1 <- c(perc_var_comp1, eigen[[i]][1,2])
}
df.unim <- data.frame(order_blocks,
```

### Paths coeffs

Pour le modèle intermédiaire, on retire le lien Y ~ Animals car le path coeff est proche de 0.

```{r, echo = TRUE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE}

model_simple <- paste(
  paste("Y =~", colnames(dfPC1.AMR_EHPAD_C3G)[1]),
  "AMC =~ log_AMC_EHPAD_C3G + log_AMC_ville_totale",
  "Animals =~ AMR_animaux_production_C3G_R + tx_possession_chats + log_UGB_density_volailles + tx_possession_chevaux",
  "Environment =~ dju_refroi + air_PM25_pop",
  "Humans =~ medecin_hab + pop_75_plus_prop",
  "Y ~ AMC + Animals + Environment + Humans",
  sep = "\n\t\t"
)

model_complet <- paste(
  paste("Y =~", colnames(dfPC1.AMR_EHPAD_C3G)[1]),
  "AMC =~ log_AMC_EHPAD_C3G + log_AMC_ville_totale",
  "Animals =~ AMR_animaux_production_C3G_R + tx_possession_chats + log_UGB_density_volailles + tx_possession_chevaux",
  "Environment =~ dju_refroi + air_PM25_pop",
  "Humans =~ medecin_hab + pop_75_plus_prop",
  "Y ~ AMC + Animals + Environment + Humans",
  "AMC ~ Humans + Environment",
  "Environment ~ Animals + Humans",
  "Humans ~ Environment + Animals",
  "Animals ~ Environment + Humans",
  sep = "\n\t\t"
)

model_int <- paste(
  paste("Y =~", colnames(dfPC1.AMR_EHPAD_C3G)[1]),
  "AMC =~ log_AMC_EHPAD_C3G + log_AMC_ville_totale",
  "Animals =~ AMR_animaux_production_C3G_R + tx_possession_chats + log_UGB_density_volailles + tx_possession_chevaux",
  "Environment =~ dju_refroi + air_PM25_pop",
  "Humans =~ medecin_hab + pop_75_plus_prop",
  "Y ~ AMC + Environment + Humans",
  "AMC ~ Humans + Environment",
  "Environment ~ Animals + Humans",
  "Humans ~ Environment + Animals",
  "Animals ~ Environment + Humans",
  sep = "\n\t\t"
)


set.seed(123)
mod_complet <- gesca::gesca.run(model_complet, dfPC1.AMR_EHPAD_C3G, nbt = 100)
sum_gsca_complet <- summary_gesca2(mod_complet)
mod_simple <- gesca::gesca.run(model_simple, dfPC1.AMR_EHPAD_C3G, nbt = 100)
sum_gsca_simple <- summary_gesca2(mod_simple)
mod_int <- gesca::gesca.run(model_int, dfPC1.AMR_EHPAD_C3G, nbt = 15)
sum_gsca_int <- summary_gesca2(mod_int)

paths_complet <- sum_gsca_complet$paths
paths_complet$model <- rep("complet", nrow(paths_complet))
paths_simple <- sum_gsca_simple$paths
paths_simple$model <- rep("simple", nrow(paths_simple))
paths_int <- sum_gsca_int$paths
paths_int$model <- rep("int", nrow(paths_int))
paths <- rbind.data.frame(paths_complet, paths_simple, paths_int)

DT::datatable(paths)

```

```{r, echo = TRUE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE}

paths$outcome <- str_remove(paths$term, "~.*")

outcomes <- unique(paths$outcome)
pal <- setNames(c("#F8766D", "#00BF7D", "#E76BF3", 
                  "#A3A500", "#00B0F6"), outcomes)

term_outcome_map <- setNames(paths$outcome, paths$term)
term_levels <- sort(unique(paths$term)) 
# applique 0.6 d'opacité à chaque couleur de la palette
pal_alpha <- scales::alpha(pal, 0.6)
strip_colors <- pal_alpha[term_outcome_map[term_levels]]


ggplot(paths, aes(x = model, y = estimate)) +
    geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = ci_lb, ymax = ci_ub, color = "95% CI"),
                   height = 0.1, alpha = 0.4) +
    geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = estimate - std.error,
                       ymax = estimate + std.error,
                       color = "+/- SE"),
                   height = 0.1, linewidth = 0.4, alpha = 0.4) +
    geom_point(aes(shape = model), size = 2) +
    geom_text(aes(label = round(estimate, 2)), 
              size = 2, vjust = -0.86)+
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
    ggh4x::facet_wrap2(~ term, scales = "free", 
                       strip = strip_themed(
      background_x = elem_list_rect(fill = strip_colors)
    ))+
    theme_bw() +
    labs(title = "Path coefficients with 95% CI and ±SE")+
    theme(axis.text = element_text(color = "black", size = 6),
          axis.title = element_blank(), 
          plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 7),
          strip.text = element_text(size = 6))+
  scale_color_manual(name = "Interval type",
                     values = c(
                       "95% CI" = "orange3",
                       "+/- SE" = "grey40"))

```

### R2

```{r, echo = TRUE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE}

# corrélations entre composantes latentes
# complet
latentcorr_complet <- mod_complet$latentcorr  
rownames(latentcorr_complet) <- c("Y", "AMC", "Animals", "Environment", "Humans")
colnames(latentcorr_complet) <- c("Y", "AMC", "Animals", "Environment", "Humans")
# int
latentcorr_int <- mod_int$latentcorr  
rownames(latentcorr_int) <- c("Y", "AMC", "Animals", "Environment", "Humans")
colnames(latentcorr_int) <- c("Y", "AMC", "Animals", "Environment", "Humans")
# simple
latentcorr_simple <- mod_simple$latentcorr  
rownames(latentcorr_simple) <- c("Y", "AMC", "Animals", "Environment", "Humans")
colnames(latentcorr_simple) <- c("Y", "AMC", "Animals", "Environment", "Humans")

R2 <- data.frame(term = sum_gsca_complet$paths$term, 
                 R2_model_complet = rep(NA, length(sum_gsca_complet$paths$term)),
                 R2_model_int = rep(NA, length(sum_gsca_complet$paths$term)), 
                 R2_model_simple = rep(NA, length(sum_gsca_complet$paths$term)))

for (i in 1:nrow(R2)){
  # complet
  beta_comp_block <- sum_gsca_complet$paths$estimate[sum_gsca_complet$paths$term == R2$term[i]]
r_block_comp <- latentcorr_complet[stringr::str_split(R2$term[i], "~")[[1]][1], stringr::str_split(R2$term[i], "~")[[1]][2]]
R2[i,]$R2_model_complet <- beta_comp_block * r_block_comp
# intermédiaire
if (R2$term[i] %in% sum_gsca_int$paths$term){
beta_int_block <- sum_gsca_int$paths$estimate[sum_gsca_int$paths$term == R2$term[i]]
r_block_int <- latentcorr_int[stringr::str_split(R2$term[i], "~")[[1]][1], stringr::str_split(R2$term[i], "~")[[1]][2]]
R2[i,]$R2_model_int <- beta_int_block * r_block_int}
else {R2[i,]$R2_model_int <- NA}
# simple
if (R2$term[i] %in% sum_gsca_simple$paths$term){
beta_simple_block <- sum_gsca_simple$paths$estimate[sum_gsca_simple$paths$term == R2$term[i]]
r_block_simple <- latentcorr_simple[stringr::str_split(R2$term[i], "~")[[1]][1], stringr::str_split(R2$term[i], "~")[[1]][2]]
R2[i,]$R2_model_simple <- beta_simple_block * r_block_simple}
else {R2[i,]$R2_model_simple <- NA}
}

knitr::kable(R2, digits = 2)



# Les R2 par blocs
r2 <- data.frame(
  var = c("Y", "AMC", "Animals", "Environment", "Humans"),
  R2_model_complet = round(mod_complet$R2[1,], 2),
  R2_model_int = round(mod_int$R2[1,], 2),
  R2_model_simple = round(mod_simple$R2[1,], 2)
)

knitr::kable(r2)

```

```{r, echo = TRUE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE}
  "Animals ~ Environment + Humans")

tab_ridge <- sum_gsca_int$paths %>% 
  dplyr::select(term, path_coeff = estimate) %>% 
  dplyr::arrange(desc(term))

# Application à tous les submodels + assemblage
ridge_results <- purrr::map_dfr(submodels, get_ridge_betas, data = latent_coord)

# Jointure avec ton tableau initial
tab_ridge <- tab_ridge %>%
  dplyr::left_join(ridge_results, by = "term")

knitr::kable(tab_ridge, digits = 2)

# Appliquer à tous les liens

  set_names(terms)

wrap_plots(plot_list, ncol = 3) + 
  plot_layout(guides = "collect") & 
  theme(legend.position = "bottom") &
  guides(col = guide_legend(nrow = 2, override.aes = list(size = 1.6)))
```

## AMR ES C3G{.tabset}

### Unidimensionalité des blocks

Le block "Animals" n'a pas l'air unidimensionnel.

```{r, echo = TRUE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE}

dfPC1.AMR_ES_C3G <- scale(dfPC1.AMR_ES_C3G) # standardisation

# Hypothèse d'unidimensionalité des blocks
Xnorm.block <- list(dfPC1.AMR_ES_C3G[,which(colnames(dfPC1.AMR_ES_C3G) %in% c("log_AMC_ES_C3G", "log_AMC_ville_C3G"))],
                    dfPC1.AMR_ES_C3G[,which(colnames(dfPC1.AMR_ES_C3G) %in% c("AMR_animaux_production_C3G_R", "tx_possession_chats", "log_UGB_density_livestock_tot
", "log_UGB_density_volailles"))],
                    dfPC1.AMR_ES_C3G[,which(colnames(dfPC1.AMR_ES_C3G) %in% c("air_PM25_pop", "dju_refroi"))],
                    dfPC1.AMR_ES_C3G[,which(colnames(dfPC1.AMR_ES_C3G) %in% c("medecin_hab", "tx_pauvrete_60"))]
                    )

nb.block <- length(Xnorm.block)
order_blocks <- c("AMC", "Animals", "Environment", "Humans")
eigen <- lapply(1:nb.block, function(k) FactoMineR::PCA(Xnorm.block[[k]], scale.unit = TRUE, ncp = 2, graph = F)$eig)
perc_var_comp1 <- c()
for(i in 1:nb.block){
  perc_var_comp1 <- c(perc_var_comp1, eigen[[i]][1,2])
}
df.unim <- data.frame(order_blocks, 
                      percentage_variance_PCA_comp1 = round(perc_var_comp1, 2))
knitr::kable(df.unim)

```

### Paths coeffs

Pour le modèle intermédiaire, on retire le lien Y ~ Animals car le path coeff est proche de 0.

```{r, echo = TRUE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE}

model_simple <- paste(
  paste("Y =~", colnames(dfPC1.AMR_ES_C3G)[1]),
  "AMC =~ log_AMC_ES_C3G + log_AMC_ville_C3G",
  "Animals =~ AMR_animaux_production_C3G_R + tx_possession_chats + log_UGB_density_volailles + log_UGB_density_livestock_tot",
  "Environment =~ dju_refroi + air_PM25_pop",
  "Humans =~ medecin_hab + tx_pauvrete_60",
  "Y ~ AMC + Animals + Environment + Humans",
  sep = "\n\t\t"
)

model_complet <- paste(
  paste("Y =~", colnames(dfPC1.AMR_ES_C3G)[1]),
  "AMC =~ log_AMC_ES_C3G + log_AMC_ville_C3G",
  "Animals =~ AMR_animaux_production_C3G_R + tx_possession_chats + log_UGB_density_volailles + log_UGB_density_livestock_tot",
  "Environment =~ dju_refroi + air_PM25_pop",
  "Humans =~ medecin_hab + tx_pauvrete_60",
  "Y ~ AMC + Animals + Environment + Humans",
  "AMC ~ Humans + Environment",
  "Environment ~ Animals + Humans",
  "Humans ~ Environment + Animals",
  "Animals ~ Environment + Humans",
  sep = "\n\t\t"
)


set.seed(123)
mod_complet <- gesca::gesca.run(model_complet, dfPC1.AMR_ES_C3G, nbt = 100)
sum_gsca_complet <- summary_gesca2(mod_complet)
mod_simple <- gesca::gesca.run(model_simple, dfPC1.AMR_ES_C3G, nbt = 100)
sum_gsca_simple <- summary_gesca2(mod_simple)

paths_complet <- sum_gsca_complet$paths
paths_complet$model <- rep("complet", nrow(paths_complet))
paths_simple <- sum_gsca_simple$paths
paths_simple$model <- rep("simple", nrow(paths_simple))
paths <- rbind.data.frame(paths_complet, paths_simple)

DT::datatable(paths)

```

```{r, echo = TRUE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE}

paths$outcome <- str_remove(paths$term, "~.*")

outcomes <- unique(paths$outcome)
pal <- setNames(c("#F8766D", "#00BF7D", "#E76BF3", 
                  "#A3A500", "#00B0F6"), outcomes)

term_outcome_map <- setNames(paths$outcome, paths$term)
term_levels <- sort(unique(paths$term)) 
# applique 0.6 d'opacité à chaque couleur de la palette
pal_alpha <- scales::alpha(pal, 0.6)
strip_colors <- pal_alpha[term_outcome_map[term_levels]]


ggplot(paths, aes(x = model, y = estimate)) +
    geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = ci_lb, ymax = ci_ub, color = "95% CI"),
                   height = 0.1, alpha = 0.4) +
    geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = estimate - std.error,
                       ymax = estimate + std.error,
                       color = "+/- SE"),
                   height = 0.1, linewidth = 0.4, alpha = 0.4) +
    geom_point(aes(shape = model), size = 2) +
    geom_text(aes(label = round(estimate, 2)), 
              size = 2, vjust = -0.86)+
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
    ggh4x::facet_wrap2(~ term, scales = "free", 
                       strip = strip_themed(
      background_x = elem_list_rect(fill = strip_colors)
    ))+
    theme_bw() +
    labs(title = "Path coefficients with 95% CI and ±SE")+
    theme(axis.text = element_text(color = "black", size = 6),
          axis.title = element_blank(), 
          plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 7),
          strip.text = element_text(size = 6))+
  scale_color_manual(name = "Interval type",
                     values = c(
                       "95% CI" = "orange3",
                       "+/- SE" = "grey40"))

```

### R2

```{r, echo = TRUE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE}

# corrélations entre composantes latentes
# complet
latentcorr_complet <- mod_complet$latentcorr  
rownames(latentcorr_complet) <- c("Y", "AMC", "Animals", "Environment", "Humans")
colnames(latentcorr_complet) <- c("Y", "AMC", "Animals", "Environment", "Humans")
# simple
latentcorr_simple <- mod_simple$latentcorr  
rownames(latentcorr_simple) <- c("Y", "AMC", "Animals", "Environment", "Humans")
colnames(latentcorr_simple) <- c("Y", "AMC", "Animals", "Environment", "Humans")

R2 <- data.frame(term = sum_gsca_complet$paths$term, 
                 R2_model_complet = rep(NA, length(sum_gsca_complet$paths$term)),
                 R2_model_simple = rep(NA, length(sum_gsca_complet$paths$term)))

for (i in 1:nrow(R2)){
  # complet
  beta_comp_block <- sum_gsca_complet$paths$estimate[sum_gsca_complet$paths$term == R2$term[i]]
r_block_comp <- latentcorr_complet[stringr::str_split(R2$term[i], "~")[[1]][1], stringr::str_split(R2$term[i], "~")[[1]][2]]
R2[i,]$R2_model_complet <- beta_comp_block * r_block_comp
# simple
if (R2$term[i] %in% sum_gsca_simple$paths$term){
beta_simple_block <- sum_gsca_simple$paths$estimate[sum_gsca_simple$paths$term == R2$term[i]]
r_block_simple <- latentcorr_simple[stringr::str_split(R2$term[i], "~")[[1]][1], stringr::str_split(R2$term[i], "~")[[1]][2]]
R2[i,]$R2_model_simple <- beta_simple_block * r_block_simple}
else {R2[i,]$R2_model_simple <- NA}
}

knitr::kable(R2, digits = 2)



# Les R2 par blocs
r2 <- data.frame(
  var = c("Y", "AMC", "Animals", "Environment", "Humans"),
  R2_model_complet = round(mod_complet$R2[1,], 2),
  R2_model_simple = round(mod_simple$R2[1,], 2)
)

knitr::kable(r2)

```

```{r, echo = TRUE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE}
#-----------------------
# construire le dataset
#-----------------------

# les paths
paths$from <- str_remove(paths$term, ".*~")
paths2 <- paths %>% 
  dplyr::rename(to = "outcome") %>% 
  dplyr::select(from, to, estimate, model) %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(sign = ifelse(estimate >=0, "pos", "neg")) %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(block = from) %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(type = "path.coeff")
# les weights
weights2 <- weights %>% 
  dplyr::rename(from = "term", to = "block") %>% 
  dplyr::select(from, to, estimate, model) %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(sign = ifelse(estimate >=0, "pos", "neg")) %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(block = to) %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(type = "weight")
# les loadings
loadings2 <- loadings %>% 
  dplyr::rename(from = "block", to = "term") %>% 
  dplyr::select(from, to, estimate, model) %>%
```

```{r, echo = TRUE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE}
Xnorm.block <- list(dfPC1.AMR_ville_C3G[,which(colnames(dfPC1.AMR_ville_C3G) %in% c("log_AMC_ES_C3G", "log_AMC_ville_totale"))],
                    dfPC1.AMR_ville_C3G[,which(colnames(dfPC1.AMR_ville_C3G) %in% c("AMR_animaux_production_C3G_R", "AMR_animaux_compagnie_amoxi_clav_R", "log_UGB_density_livestock_tot", "veto_by_CV"))],
                    dfPC1.AMR_ville_C3G[,which(colnames(dfPC1.AMR_ville_C3G) %in% c("air_PM25_pop", "dju_refroi"))],
                    dfPC1.AMR_ville_C3G[,which(colnames(dfPC1.AMR_ville_C3G) %in% c("medecin_hab", "tx_pauvrete_60"))]
                    )

nb.block <- length(Xnorm.block)
order_blocks <- c("AMC", "Animals", "Environment", "Humans")
eigen <- lapply(1:nb.block, function(k) FactoMineR::PCA(Xnorm.block[[k]], scale.unit = TRUE, ncp = 2, graph = F)$eig)
perc_var_comp1 <- c()
for(i in 1:nb.block){
  perc_var_comp1 <- c(perc_var_comp1, eigen[[i]][1,2])
}
df.unim <- data.frame(order_blocks, 
                      percentage_variance_PCA_comp1 = round(perc_var_comp1, 2))
knitr::kable(df.unim)

```

### Paths coeffs

```{r, echo = TRUE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE}

model_simple <- paste(
 paste("Y =~", colnames(dfPC1.AMR_ville_C3G)[1]),
  "AMC =~ log_AMC_ES_C3G + log_AMC_ville_totale",
  "Animals =~ AMR_animaux_production_C3G_R + AMR_animaux_compagnie_amoxi_clav_R + log_UGB_density_volailles + veto_by_CV",
  "Environment =~ dju_refroi + air_PM25_pop",
  "Humans =~ medecin_hab + tx_pauvrete_60",
  "Y ~ AMC + Animals + Environment + Humans",
  sep = "\n\t\t"
)

model_complet <- paste(
  paste("Y =~", colnames(dfPC1.AMR_ville_C3G)[1]),
  "AMC =~ log_AMC_ES_C3G + log_AMC_ville_totale",
  "Animals =~ AMR_animaux_production_C3G_R + AMR_animaux_compagnie_amoxi_clav_R + log_UGB_density_volailles + veto_by_CV",
  "Environment =~ dju_refroi + air_PM25_pop",
  "Humans =~ medecin_hab + tx_pauvrete_60",
  "Y ~ AMC + Animals + Environment + Humans",
  "AMC ~ Humans + Environment",
  "Environment ~ Animals + Humans",
  "Humans ~ Environment + Animals",
  "Animals ~ Environment + Humans",
  sep = "\n\t\t"
)


set.seed(123)
mod_complet <- gesca::gesca.run(model_complet, dfPC1.AMR_ville_C3G, nbt = 100)
sum_gsca_complet <- summary_gesca2(mod_complet)
mod_simple <- gesca::gesca.run(model_simple, dfPC1.AMR_ville_C3G, nbt = 100)
sum_gsca_simple <- summary_gesca2(mod_simple)

paths_complet <- sum_gsca_complet$paths
paths_complet$model <- rep("complet", nrow(paths_complet))
paths_simple <- sum_gsca_simple$paths
paths_simple$model <- rep("simple", nrow(paths_simple))
paths <- rbind.data.frame(paths_complet, paths_simple)

DT::datatable(paths)

```

```{r, echo = TRUE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE}

paths$outcome <- str_remove(paths$term, "~.*")

outcomes <- unique(paths$outcome)
pal <- setNames(c("#F8766D", "#00BF7D", "#E76BF3", 
                  "#A3A500", "#00B0F6"), outcomes)

term_outcome_map <- setNames(paths$outcome, paths$term)
term_levels <- sort(unique(paths$term)) 
# applique 0.6 d'opacité à chaque couleur de la palette
pal_alpha <- scales::alpha(pal, 0.6)
strip_colors <- pal_alpha[term_outcome_map[term_levels]]


ggplot(paths, aes(x = model, y = estimate)) +
    geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = ci_lb, ymax = ci_ub, color = "95% CI"),
                   height = 0.1, alpha = 0.4) +
    geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = estimate - std.error,
                       ymax = estimate + std.error,
                       color = "+/- SE"),
                   height = 0.1, linewidth = 0.4, alpha = 0.4) +
    geom_point(aes(shape = model), size = 2) +
    geom_text(aes(label = round(estimate, 2)), 
              size = 2, vjust = -0.86)+
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
    ggh4x::facet_wrap2(~ term, scales = "free", 
                       strip = strip_themed(
      background_x = elem_list_rect(fill = strip_colors)
    ))+
    theme_bw() +
    labs(title = "Path coefficients with 95% CI and ±SE")+
    theme(axis.text = element_text(color = "black", size = 6),
          axis.title = element_blank(), 
          plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 7),
          strip.text = element_text(size = 6))+
  scale_color_manual(name = "Interval type",
                     values = c(
                       "95% CI" = "orange3",
                       "+/- SE" = "grey40"))

```

### R2

```{r, echo = TRUE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE}

# corrélations entre composantes latentes
# complet
latentcorr_complet <- mod_complet$latentcorr  
rownames(latentcorr_complet) <- c("Y", "AMC", "Animals", "Environment", "Humans")
colnames(latentcorr_complet) <- c("Y", "AMC", "Animals", "Environment", "Humans")
# simple
latentcorr_simple <- mod_simple$latentcorr  
rownames(latentcorr_simple) <- c("Y", "AMC", "Animals", "Environment", "Humans")
colnames(latentcorr_simple) <- c("Y", "AMC", "Animals", "Environment", "Humans")

R2 <- data.frame(term = sum_gsca_complet$paths$term, 
                 R2_model_complet = rep(NA, length(sum_gsca_complet$paths$term)),
                 R2_model_simple = rep(NA, length(sum_gsca_complet$paths$term)))

for (i in 1:nrow(R2)){
  # complet
  beta_comp_block <- sum_gsca_complet$paths$estimate[sum_gsca_complet$paths$term == R2$term[i]]
r_block_comp <- latentcorr_complet[stringr::str_split(R2$term[i], "~")[[1]][1], stringr::str_split(R2$term[i], "~")[[1]][2]]
R2[i,]$R2_model_complet <- beta_comp_block * r_block_comp
# simple
if (R2$term[i] %in% sum_gsca_simple$paths$term){
beta_simple_block <- sum_gsca_simple$paths$estimate[sum_gsca_simple$paths$term == R2$term[i]]
r_block_simple <- latentcorr_simple[stringr::str_split(R2$term[i], "~")[[1]][1], stringr::str_split(R2$term[i], "~")[[1]][2]]
R2[i,]$R2_model_simple <- beta_simple_block * r_block_simple}
else {R2[i,]$R2_model_simple <- NA}
}

knitr::kable(R2, digits = 2)



# Les R2 par blocs
r2 <- data.frame(
  var = c("Y", "AMC", "Animals", "Environment", "Humans"),
  R2_model_complet = round(mod_complet$R2[1,], 2),
  R2_model_simple = round(mod_simple$R2[1,], 2)
)

knitr::kable(r2)

```

### graphes

```{r, echo = TRUE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE}

#-----------------------
# construire le dataset
#-----------------------

# les paths
paths$from <- str_remove(paths$term, ".*~")
paths2 <- paths %>% 
  dplyr::rename(to = "outcome") %>% 
  dplyr::select(from, to, estimate, model) %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(sign = ifelse(estimate >=0, "pos", "neg")) %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(block = from) %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(type = "path.coeff")
# les weights
weights2 <- weights %>% 
  dplyr::rename(from = "term", to = "block") %>% 
  dplyr::select(from, to, estimate, model) %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(sign = ifelse(estimate >=0, "pos", "neg")) %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(block = to) %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(type = "weight")
# les loadings
loadings2 <- loadings %>% 
  dplyr::rename(from = "block", to = "term") %>% 
  dplyr::select(from, to, estimate, model) %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(sign = ifelse(estimate >=0, "pos", "neg")) %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(block = from) %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(type = "loading")

dat_graph <- rbind(paths2, weights2, loadings2)

#----------------------
# modèle complet
#----------------------

dat_filtered <- dat_graph %>% 
  dplyr::filter(model == "complet")

# Construire le tableau des noeuds avec leur block
nodes_df <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  dat_filtered %>% dplyr::select(name = from, block),
  dat_filtered %>% dplyr::select(name = to, block)
) %>% 
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(block)) %>%   # garde les lignes où block est renseigné
  dplyr::distinct(name, .keep_all = TRUE)  # une ligne par noeud

# Construire le graphe explicitement
graph <- tbl_graph(
  nodes = nodes_df,
  edges = dat_filtered %>% dplyr::select(from, to, estimate, sign, type),
  node_key = "name"
)

  geom_edge_fan(aes(colour = sign,
                     end_cap = label_rect(node2.name),

  labs(title = "modèle complet")+
  scale_x_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = 0.10)) +
  ggraph::theme_graph(background = 'white') +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom") +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 10))+
  scale_edge_colour_manual(values = c("darkred", "darkgreen"))+
  scale_edge_linetype_manual(values = c(path.coeff = "solid", weight = "dashed", loading = "dotted"))+
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(Y = "#F8766D", Animals = "#00B0F6", Humans = "#E76BF3", 
                  Environment = "#00BF7D", AMC = "#A3A500"))
```
